content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through iteration utilities with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns $.each() into a repeatable implementation choice. Static jQuery utilities help process values and collections, but current JavaScript already provides Array, Object, Map, Set, and String APIs. Prefer the clearest supported API.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
